title: Cloudflare, July 2 2019: a WAF rule pins every CPU, 27-minute global outage
what_happened: A new managed WAF rule shipped with a regular expression whose `.*(?:.*=.*)` part backtracks super-linearly. Rules deploy globally at once, so every edge server's CPU went to 100% matching HTTP requests against it.
sources: Cloudflare blog, "Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019" (July 12 2019), which quotes the regex
language: Python port (Cloudflare's WAF ran PCRE from Lua); the regex is verbatim.

damage.label: of global outage: Cloudflare's proxy, CDN and WAF down (13:42 to 14:09 UTC)
of Cloudflare's traffic lost at the worst point
CPU on the servers handling HTTP and HTTPS traffic

catch.says: The new pattern ends in .*(?:.*=.*): three unbounded parts that can match the same characters, so on a long request the regex engine tries a super-linear number of ways to split it.
catch.fix: Drop the redundant .* parts or bound them, and time the pattern on long inputs before it ships.

steps.what: The new XSS rule, with the regex from Cloudflare's post-mortem.
